description.p: Wflow is a lightweight native dictation studio written in Rust. It captures your microphone, streams it to a speech-to-text provider of your choice and pastes the transcript straight into the focused text box.

ul.li: Multiple speech-to-text engines: Wispr Flow (gRPC streaming), Groq Whisper and ElevenLabs Scribe
Global push-to-talk hotkey with full modifier combinations
Floating HUD overlay with a live microphone waveform
Optional AI post-processing for punctuation, cleanup and formatting
Local SQLite history plus a personal vocabulary and snippet dictionary
System tray integration, auto-start and an in-app update checker
Nothing is sent to the provider when the noise gate heard no speech
The gRPC session is only opened once real speech has been captured
A clear message explains why nothing was inserted
Silence filter / noise gate: only speech is sent to the model
Hallucination guard: blocks "Thank you.", "(music)" and other model garbage
Per-language automatic spell check (offline dictionary + LLM)
Mixed Thai/Latin spacing is fixed automatically
Live voice-activity indicator in the studio
A visible update button in the top bar, on every tab
Clickable version indicator in the sidebar
"Check for updates" entry in the system tray menu
Periodic background update checks while the app is running
Fixed the status and focus pills painting over their own text
Patch the rustls-webpki and webpki-roots advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0381/0382)
Share one virtual-key naming table across every platform backend
Update arboard, x11rb and rusqlite
Credentials are stored in a separate 0600 secrets file instead of the config file
The embedded gateway key has been removed; supply your own
Privacy controls for text-context sharing and local history retention
Native global hotkeys on Linux (X11/XWayland)
Floating HUD on Linux, earcon playback on Linux and macOS
Diagnostic log files, single-instance guard and graceful shutdown
In-app update checker with release notes and platform download links
